Hi Tina / James —

Thanks for sending over your MSA. Connor looped me in; I lead commercial contracts for Redwood. I attached a clean version of our proposed compromise language and a short summary of changes we think are reasonable for a pilot scope. High-level summary:

- Output ownership: Redwood proposes customers retain rights to customer-provided input and generated outputs for their internal use; Redwood requests a narrow, non-commercial license to use output for the sole purpose of debugging, improving service, and aggregate analytics, with no right to sell customer-derived outputs.

- Training/data use: For production pilots, we cannot accept broad training licenses that allow model retraining on raw customer data. We offer:
  * Option A (preferred): No training on raw input or output without explicit opt-in. Aggregate, de-identified telemetry may be used for service improvement.
  * Option B: Time-limited training license for specific datasets with explicit approval and standard data protection controls.

- Feedback: We propose a simple royalty-free feedback license for suggestions and bug reports, limited to improving the platform.

Please see the attached redline (Acme_MSA_redline_20270410.docx). I highlighted the replacement text next to the original clauses. If you prefer, we can propose exact sentence-level edits in the doc or walk through on the call.

Our ask: confirmation on whether Acme can accept Option A for the pilot. If you need a limited training carveout, indicate which subsets of data (e.g., anonymized usage logs only) are in scope.

If it helps, Connor and I can prepare a one-page clause that legal can present to their GC.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: Acme_MSA_redline_20270410.docx (redlines inline)

Subject: Re: ACME MSA — IP use and training carveouts (coordination)

Laura / Connor —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the summary. A couple of points from Acme Legal / Product that will likely be non-starters without narrower language or specific carveouts:

1) Output ownership: Acme insists that outputs derived from our customer data be owned by Acme (to enable downstream productization). We are open to granting Redwood a narrow operational license but cannot accept language that lets Redwood use outputs for improving models that Acme might compete with internally.

2) Training/data use: Our GC will push back on Option A unless we can get an exception for aggregated model improvements that help latency/quality across all customers. Also we need a clear audit trail and the ability to opt-out of any training use for certain high-risk datasets (PII / regulated customer content).

3) Feedback: We are okay with a feedback license but need an explicit carveout that excludes technical suggestions that are uniquely derived from Acme's proprietary prompts and fine-tuning recipes.

Can you send concrete sentence-level alternative text for each clause we flagged? Also please include an example of the narrow operational license you're proposing (scope, duration, and no-commercialization language). Our GC is reviewing and wants to see precise wording before the Wednesday procurement sync.

Thanks —
Tina Wu
Head of Product Legal
Acme Inc.

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Tina Wu <tina.wu@acme.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 13:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME MSA — IP use and training carveouts (coordination)

Thanks Tina — good, actionable feedback. Laura and I discussed and drafted precise language below that we think addresses Acme's concerns while preserving Redwood's need to operate and improve the service. Please review and let us know which parts are acceptable. If helpful we can add an explicit opt-out checkbox on the order form that toggles any training use for the account.

Proposed language snippets (draft):

Section 6 (Customer Data and Output Ownership) — Draft: "Customer retains all right, title and interest in and to Customer Data and any Outputs generated by the Service using Customer Data. Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, revocable, worldwide license to use Outputs solely for the purposes of (a) providing the Service to Customer; (b) troubleshooting and debugging requests from Customer; and (c) generating aggregated, de-identified metrics for service reliability and performance. Redwood shall not use Customer Data or Outputs to train models used to provide services to third parties or to create derivative products for resale without Customer's prior written consent."

Section 11 (Training and Model Improvements) — Draft: "Redwood shall not use raw Customer Data or Outputs to train or fine-tune production models without Customer's explicit opt-in. Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry (e.g., latency statistics, anonymized token-level frequencies) to improve platform stability and performance, provided such telemetry cannot be reasonably re-identified and is subject to the parties' Data Protection Addendum. For accounts that opt-in, any training on Customer Data shall be limited to mutually agreed datasets, limited duration, and governed by a separate training schedule and security annex."

Section 14 (Feedback License) — Draft: "Customer hereby grants Redwood a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, non-exclusive license to use Feedback (as defined below) to improve Redwood's products and services, provided that Feedback does not include, and Redwood shall not use, Customer Confidential Information, proprietary prompts, or fine-tuning recipes unique to Customer without separate written permission from Customer. Feedback means suggestions, bug reports, and feature requests submitted by Customer's users or representatives."

Next steps I propose:
- Laura to produce a tracked-change redline with these snippets inline (we can do this by EOD).
- Connor to add Order Form opt-in checkbox language for training and a short definition of "aggregated, de-identified telemetry".
- Tina/Acme to indicate whether their GC prefers a checkbox opt-out/opt-in or a contract-level carveout.

If these look close, we can table this as the legal path forward and get procurement to accept the pilot with an opt-in for training.

Connor
Senior AE, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
